Q: How to summarise hourly data of the Formal class 'Period' using dplyr and lubridate? A:

When I run the group by, it groups by hour just fine

df %>% group_by(time) %>% summarise(total = sum(outcome))

returns

   time     total
   <Period> <dbl>
 1 0S          52
 2 1H 0M 0S    52
 3 2H 0M 0S    44
 4 3H 0M 0S    52
 5 4H 0M 0S    50
 6 5H 0M 0S    56
 7 6H 0M 0S    38
 8 7H 0M 0S    47
 9 8H 0M 0S    51
10 9H 0M 0S    49
# ℹ 14 more rows

if you use set.seed(101) before generating the sample data.

If you had data that had seconds but you wanted to round only to the full hour, you could use the hour() function form lubridate to get the hour part of the period

df |> group_by(hour(time)) |> summarize(sum(outcome))

which gives

   `hour(time)` `sum(outcome)`
          <dbl>          <dbl>
 1            0             52
 2            1             52
 3            2             44
 4            3             52
 5            4             50
 6            5             56
 7            6             38
 8            7             47
 9            8             51
10            9             49

That does change the hour to an int. If you wanted to round the value but keep it a Period, you could use

df |> group_by(hours(hour(time))) |> summarize(sum(outcome))

to get

   time     total
   <Period> <dbl>
 1 0S          52
 2 1H 0M 0S    52
 3 2H 0M 0S    44
 4 3H 0M 0S    52
 5 4H 0M 0S    50
 6 5H 0M 0S    56
 7 6H 0M 0S    38
 8 7H 0M 0S    47
 9 8H 0M 0S    51
10 9H 0M 0S    49
# ℹ 14 more rows

Tested with dplyr_1.2.1 and lubridate_1.9.5

Q: How can I reliably test the Google Play Age Signals requestAgeSignalsAccess() prompt? A:

Short answer: there's no supported way to force the "Ask before sharing" prompt on demand — it's gated by a server-side regional rollout, not a local toggle, and your test accounts almost certainly aren't in an eligible cohort yet.

1. Why your Texas account didn't work - Version 0.0.3 of the API has started returning age signals for eligible users in Texas only for accounts created after May 28, 2026, as part of compliance with Texas SB2420. If your Texas test account predates the law, it's excluded by design — that's specifically the eligibility rule, not a bug. You'd need a Texas account created after that date to reproduce mandatory-verification behavior there. (Worth noting separately: some coverage indicates Texas responses were paused for a period due to a legal injunction, so even a post-May-28 account isn't guaranteed to behave consistently right now — it's worth re-checking current status rather than assuming it's stable.)

2. Why the optional "Ask before sharing" flow isn't appearing anywhere - As of the current docs, the API only returns signals for users in Brazil (since March 17, 2026, under Digital ECA) and eligible Texas users (since May 28, 2026, under SB2420), with further US states being rolled out ahead of their respective law dates. Separately, Google announced a global expansion of the API on July 29, 2026, and said it was already live in Brazil with Australia and Canada set to follow by mid-August 2026, with the rest of supported markets completing later in 2026.

That's the key point: the voluntary "Ask before sharing" flow (and the corresponding Age range sharing entry under Play Store → Settings → Family) is being turned on region-by-region on Google's side. If your test accounts aren't in one of the currently-enabled regions, the setting simply won't exist yet for those accounts — it's not something your app, your device, or your account settings can force into existence early. That matches exactly what you're seeing: NOT_SHARED with no prompt, across every account you've tried, none of which are in a currently-eligible cohort.

3. What you can actually do to test the real prompt right now

  • Get an account genuinely in an enabled region — a Brazil-region test account is your best bet today, since that's been live the longest.

  • If you need US coverage, use a Texas account created after May 28, 2026 (for the mandatory-verification path, not the optional prompt — Texas is a mandatory-verification state, so you'll see VERIFICATION_REQUIRED/SHARED behavior, not the "Ask before sharing" dialog, which only applies to non-mandatory regions).

  • Keep an eye on the release notes page and the Play Console's regulatory status info, since Australia/Canada were slated for mid-August 2026 and your account may become eligible very soon.

  • For anything before you have an eligible account, FakeAgeSignalsManager remains the only way to exercise your app's handling logic for SHARED/NOT_SHARED/VERIFICATION_REQUIRED — but as you found, it can't reproduce Play's actual in-app UI, because that UI is tied to real Play backend state for the signed-in account.

So to directly answer your key question: the missing setting means the feature hasn't been enabled for your account/region yet — it's a phased rollout, not a missing eligibility flag you can flip yourself.

Q: Italicize all but predefined strings with ggtext A:

I'm guessing that the underscores you start with in var are unrelated, since if you had wanted "A" to be italicized, you should have a leading _ before it. I think we can use another gsub to find those letters and italicize them:

i <- 1L # just to work through it locally
ggplot(data = mtcars, aes(x = mpg, y = cyl)) +
      geom_point() +
      labs(title = gsub("\\b([A-E])\\b", "_\\1_", gsub("_", " ", var[i]))) +
      theme(plot.title = element_markdown())

If you have more single-character letters to include in that "italicize" allowance, just add them to the [A-E] group. If it is easier to think of just an exception list (i.e., italicize everything except these few things), then perhaps this is more direct:

(txt <- gsub("_", " ", var[i]))
# [1] "A in B and C"
sapply(strsplit(txt, " +"), function(tx) paste(ifelse(tx %in% c("in", "and"), tx, paste0("_", tx, "_")), collapse = " "))
# [1] "_A_ in _B_ and _C_"
